recipes.title: Korean beef seaweed soup, light
recipes.summary: A light version of Korean miyeok-guk with tender beef brisket, mineral-rich seaweed and a modest serving of rice. The broth stays deeply savoury with very little added fat.

steps.instruction: Soak the seaweed in cold water until fully expanded and supple.
Drain the seaweed well and cut it into manageable pieces.
Rinse the white rice under cold water until the water runs mostly clear.
Cook the white rice until tender, then keep it covered so the grains finish steaming.
Heat the sesame oil in a large pot and brown the beef brisket lightly around the edges.
Add the garlic and cook until fragrant without letting it colour.
Stir in the seaweed until it is evenly coated with the sesame oil and beef juices.
Pour in the beef stock and simmer gently until the brisket is tender and the broth tastes well developed.
Season the soup with the salt and finish each bowl with spring onions.
Serve the Korean beef seaweed soup with the white rice alongside.

recipes.storageNotes: Refrigerate the soup for up to 3 days and the rice separately for up to 3 days. Reheat until steaming. Freeze the soup without the spring onions for up to 2 months.

recipes.title: Korean beef seaweed soup, hearty
recipes.summary: A generous pot of Korean miyeok-guk with extra beef brisket, rice and sesame aroma. Long simmering leaves the seaweed silky and the broth deeply satisfying.

steps.instruction: Soak the seaweed in cold water until fully expanded and supple.
Drain the seaweed well and cut it into manageable pieces.
Rinse the white rice under cold water until the water runs mostly clear.
Cook the white rice until tender, then keep the larger batch covered so it finishes steaming evenly.
Heat the sesame oil in a large pot and brown the beef brisket in batches.
Add the garlic and cook until fragrant without letting it colour.
Stir in the seaweed until it is thoroughly coated with the sesame oil and beef juices.

Serve the Korean beef seaweed soup with the white rice alongside.

recipes.storageNotes: Refrigerate the soup and rice separately for up to 3 days. Reheat thoroughly. Freeze the soup without the spring onions for up to 2 months.

recipes.title: Scandinavian shrimp and egg open sandwiches, light
recipes.summary: Open sandwiches topped with shrimp, boiled egg, cucumber and a cool dill yogurt spread. Thin bread and extra cucumber keep this high-protein Nordic snack fresh and light.

steps.instruction: Boil the eggs until the whites are set and the yolks are firm but still tender.
Cool the eggs in cold water until comfortable to handle.
Slice the cucumber and spring onions while the eggs cool.
Stir the greek yogurt with the dill weed and lemon juice until smooth.
Peel and slice the eggs into neat rounds.
Spread the greek yogurt mixture evenly over the bread.
Layer the shrimp, eggs and cucumber over the bread.
Finish the open sandwiches with the spring onions and serve immediately.

recipes.storageNotes: Best assembled immediately. Refrigerate the shrimp, eggs and yogurt spread separately for up to 2 days. Once assembled, the bread softens quickly and should not be frozen.

recipes.summary: Nordic-style open sandwiches with generous shrimp, sliced egg, cucumber and a tangy dill yogurt spread. They are cool, savoury and naturally high in protein.

steps.instruction: Boil the eggs until the whites are set and the yolks are tender.
Cool the eggs in cold water until comfortable to handle.
Slice the cucumber and spring onions while the eggs cool.
Stir the greek yogurt with the dill weed and lemon juice until smooth and spoonable.
Peel and slice the eggs into neat rounds.
Spread the greek yogurt mixture evenly over the bread.
Layer the shrimp, eggs and cucumber generously over the bread.
Finish the open sandwiches with the spring onions and serve immediately.

recipes.storageNotes: Keep the components refrigerated separately for up to 2 days and assemble shortly before serving. The finished sandwiches do not freeze well.

recipes.title: Scandinavian shrimp and egg open sandwiches, hearty
recipes.summary: Generous open sandwiches piled with shrimp, boiled egg and cucumber over creamy dill yogurt. Extra bread and protein make this a substantial Scandinavian snack for two.

steps.instruction: Boil the eggs until the whites and yolks are set to your liking.
Cool the eggs in cold water until comfortable to handle.
Slice the cucumber and spring onions while the eggs cool.
Stir the greek yogurt with the dill weed and lemon juice until smooth.
Peel and slice the eggs into neat rounds.
Spread the greek yogurt mixture evenly over all the bread.
Layer the shrimp, eggs and cucumber generously over the bread.
Finish the open sandwiches with the spring onions and serve immediately.

recipes.title: Thai mushroom khao tom, light
recipes.summary: A light vegan Thai rice soup with mushrooms, tofu, ginger and garlic in a savoury broth. Extra vegetables and less rice keep the breakfast warming without making it heavy.

steps.instruction: Rinse the white rice under cold water until the water runs mostly clear.
Slice the mushrooms and shiitake mushrooms and prepare the tofu, ginger, garlic, spring onions, cilantro and lime.
Heat the sesame oil in a deep saucepan and cook the ginger and garlic until fragrant.
Pour in the vegetable broth and soy sauce and bring the liquid to a gentle boil.
Add the white rice and simmer until the grains are very soft and the broth looks lightly thickened.
Add the mushrooms, shiitake mushrooms and tofu and simmer until the mushrooms are tender and the tofu is hot.
Rest the khao tom off the heat so the rice settles into the broth.
Divide the soup between bowls and finish with spring onions, cilantro and lime.

recipes.storageNotes: Refrigerate for up to 3 days and reheat with extra vegetable broth because the rice thickens while stored. Freeze for up to 1 month, though the tofu will become slightly firmer.

recipes.title: Thai mushroom khao tom
recipes.summary: Comforting Thai khao tom with soft rice, tofu and two kinds of mushrooms in a ginger-garlic broth. Soy sauce, herbs and lime give the vegan breakfast a bright savoury finish.

steps.instruction: Rinse the white rice under cold water until the water runs mostly clear.
Slice the mushrooms and shiitake mushrooms and prepare the tofu, ginger, garlic, spring onions, cilantro and lime.
Heat the sesame oil in a deep saucepan and cook the ginger and garlic until fragrant.
Pour in the vegetable broth and soy sauce and bring the liquid to a gentle boil.
Add the white rice and simmer until the grains soften and begin to thicken the broth.
Add the mushrooms, shiitake mushrooms and tofu and simmer until tender and hot throughout.
Rest the khao tom off the heat so the rice absorbs more of the savoury broth.
Divide the soup between bowls and finish with spring onions, cilantro and lime.

recipes.storageNotes: Refrigerate for up to 3 days and loosen with vegetable broth during reheating. Heat until steaming. Freeze for up to 1 month.

recipes.title: Thai mushroom khao tom, hearty
recipes.summary: A generous bowl of Thai rice soup with extra tofu, rice and mushrooms. Ginger, garlic, soy sauce, cilantro and lime keep the hearty vegan breakfast fresh and aromatic.

steps.instruction: Rinse the white rice under cold water until the water runs mostly clear.
Slice the mushrooms and shiitake mushrooms and prepare the tofu, ginger, garlic, spring onions, cilantro and lime.
Heat the sesame oil in a large saucepan and cook the ginger and garlic until fragrant.
Pour in the vegetable broth and soy sauce and bring the liquid to a gentle boil.
Add the white rice and simmer until the larger amount of rice is very soft and the broth becomes silky.
Add the mushrooms, shiitake mushrooms and tofu and simmer until the mushrooms are tender and the tofu is hot.
Rest the khao tom off the heat so the rice thickens the broth slightly.

recipes.storageNotes: Refrigerate for up to 3 days and reheat with additional vegetable broth. Freeze for up to 1 month; the tofu texture will be firmer after thawing.

recipes.title: Turkish red lentil köfte, light
recipes.summary: Soft Turkish red lentil and bulgur patties seasoned with tomato, cumin, paprika, spring onions and lemon. Less bulgur and oil keep this Mediterranean lunch light and fresh.

steps.instruction: Rinse the red lentils until the water runs mostly clear.
Simmer the red lentils in the vegetable broth until collapsed and thick.
Stir the bulgur into the hot lentils, cover the pan and leave it to soften.
Cook the onion in the olive oil until soft and translucent.
Stir the tomato paste, cumin and paprika into the onion until fragrant.
Fold the onion mixture through the red lentils and bulgur until evenly coloured.
Cool the lentil mixture until comfortable to handle.
Fold in the spring onions, cilantro and lemon juice.
Shape the mixture into small oval köfte with lightly damp hands.
Slice the cucumber and arrange it around the Turkish red lentil köfte.

recipes.storageNotes: Refrigerate for up to 3 days and serve chilled or at room temperature. Store the cucumber separately. The köfte can be frozen for up to 1 month, though the herbs will soften.

recipes.title: Vietnamese lemongrass tofu noodle bowls, light
recipes.summary: Rice noodles, crisp vegetables and golden tofu dressed with lemongrass, lime and soy sauce. Less noodles and oil keep the vegetarian dinner fresh while the tofu stays generous.

steps.instruction: Prepare the tofu, lemon grass, garlic, ginger, cucumber, carrot, spring onions, cilantro and lime.
Stir the lemon grass, garlic, ginger, soy sauce, brown sugar and half the sesame oil together.
Coat the tofu with the lemon grass mixture and leave it to absorb the seasoning.
Cook the rice noodles until tender but still springy, then drain them thoroughly.
Heat the remaining sesame oil in a wide non-stick frying pan.
Cook the tofu until golden on several sides and fragrant with lemon grass.
Divide the rice noodles, cucumber, carrot and bean sprouts between bowls.
Top the bowls with the tofu, spring onions and cilantro.
Squeeze the lime over the Vietnamese lemon grass tofu noodle bowls before serving.

recipes.storageNotes: Best assembled fresh. Refrigerate the tofu and vegetables separately for up to 3 days and the noodles for up to 2 days. Reheat only the tofu; freezing is not recommended.

recipes.title: Vietnamese lemongrass tofu noodle bowls
recipes.summary: Golden lemongrass tofu served over rice noodles with cucumber, carrot, bean sprouts, herbs and lime. The Vietnamese-style bowl is bright, savoury and completely vegetarian.

steps.instruction: Prepare the tofu, lemon grass, garlic, ginger, cucumber, carrot, spring onions, cilantro and lime.

Cook the rice noodles until tender with a slight chew, then drain them thoroughly.
Heat the remaining sesame oil in a wide non-stick frying pan.
Cook the tofu until deeply golden on several sides and fragrant with lemon grass.
Divide the rice noodles, cucumber, carrot and bean sprouts between bowls.
Top the bowls with the tofu, spring onions and cilantro.
Squeeze the lime over the Vietnamese lemon grass tofu noodle bowls before serving.

recipes.storageNotes: Refrigerate the cooked tofu and prepared vegetables separately for up to 3 days. Keep noodles for up to 2 days. Assemble after reheating the tofu. Do not freeze.
